entities.summary: Newel Kimball Whitney was a prominent member and leader in the Latter Day Saint movement and an American businessman. Born in 1795 in Kirtland, Ohio, Whitney married Elizabeth Ann Smith in 1822 and owned a store and an ashery in Kirtland, acquiring more property as his business grew. Initially he was part of the Disciples of Christ or Campbellite movement, but joined the early Latter Day Saint church, called the Church of Christ, in 1830 after his Campbellite bishop, Sidney Rigdon, also joined the church. Whitney greatly contributed to the development of the Latter Day Saint church, serving as a counselor to Joseph Smith and participating in the translation of the Book of Mormon. He played a key role in the establishment of the Kirtland Temple in 1836 and was a vocal advocate for the church's financial and economic matters. Whitney's leadership and business acumen helped shape the economic and social fabric of the Latter Day Saint community in Ohio. He died on September 23, 1850, at the age of 55, leaving behind a lasting legacy in the Latter Day Saint movement.
